Registers are devices that temporarily store and transfer data.
INTRODUCTIONM
They are manufactured as ICs and commonly have capacities of 4, 5, 8 or 16 bits.
Inputs and outputs can be serial, parallel or both. The serial or parallel outputs inputs are synchronously clocked .chronous .
DEFINITION
SYNCHRONOUS - Having a fixed time relationship. The output of a device changes state only at a specified point on a triggering input, such as the clock input to a flip-flop.
Some registers use inputs such as preset and clear that do not require clock pulses. These inputs and outputs are asynchronous.
Some registers use inputs such as preset and clear that do not require clock pulses. These inputs and outputs are asynchronous.
DEFINITION
ASYNCHRONOUS - Having no fixed time relationship. The input/output does not need a timing input. For example, the clear and preset inputs to a flip-flop are asynchronous.

An 8 bit shift register is designed to transfer eight bits of binary data from one circuit to another.
DISCUSSION
Other registers shift 4, 5 and 16 or more bits. For example, three 4 bit registers can shift 12 bits of data if connected.

Registers shift data on manual commands. For example, numbers entered into a hand held calculator.
Data shifted manually is called asynchronous . The next input occurs at any time.

DEFINITION
Registers also shift data automatically. A computer executing a program uses automatic data shifting.
Data shifted automatically is called synchronous . A specific time between inputs is controlled by a clock pulse.

Asynchronous data is shifted manually. For example, any keyboard input that waits for the next manual input is asynchronous.

This register uses both synchronous and asynchronous inputs and outputs.
Serial inputs are synchronous and controlled by the clock input.
Each clock pulse shifts data one flip-flop to the right. Serial synchronous data is available at the output.
Notice that synchronous parallel output data is available on each clock pulse at QA through QH.
Parallel inputs are asynchronous and controlled by a high applied to the Preset enable.
Parallel inputs PA through PH manually provide data inputs to the register.
Enabling the clear input resets the register. The register's content is 00000000.
When the preset input is high, a high on any P input shifts a 1 into the register. The clock is not used.
How is serial data shifted into a register?
Serial data shifts into the register one bit at a time. A clock or synchronous signal is required.
TRY AGAIN!
The preset input to a flip-flop is not dependent on a clock pulse so it is asynchronous. Serial data shifts into the register one bit at a time. A clock or synchronous signal is required.
TRY AGAIN!
How is manual parallel data shifted into a register?
Manual parallel data is not clock dependent. Synchronous inputs require a clock.
TRY AGAIN!
The D input requires a clock pulse to set or reset the flip-flop. Manual inputs do not require clock.
TRY AGAIN!
Now let's look at a typical circuit in a hand held calculator and see how different registers can be used.
Pressing a number key on the calculator shifts a binary number into register A.
The input is manual asynchronous. Parallel data is shifted in.
The parallel output of the register is sent to the display.
Pressing the + key shifts synchronous serial data from register A to register B.
The second number is then entered into register A by asynchronous parallel input.
Pressing the = key, synchronous serial data shifts from register A to register C.
The stored contents of registers B and C are serially shifted to the adder and summed.
The sum is serially shifted back to register A and then sent in parallel to the display.
This circuit used registers with asynchronous parallel inputs.
This circuit used registers with a asynchronous parallel outputs.
This circuit used registers with synchronous serial inputs.
This circuit used registers with synchronous serial outputs.
